request.spec:
A person can be retired from a date (defaults to the sheet's today). A claim dated after a person's
retirement date is refused with an error; claims dated on or before it are allowed even if added
later. Retired people are left out of the list (no row for them on the screen at all) unless "show
retired" is on: a toggle on the screen, off when the screen is first opened and left as it is by
loading a sheet. Their claims keep counting in every total. Show retired yes/no and retired-from.
Retiring writes PERSON_RETIRED name=<name> from=<date>. A person with a retirement date set counts
as retired at once, whatever the date, even one after the sheet's today: the row shows retired yes,
the list hides it, and every rule that speaks of a retired person or member applies to them.

You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person can be retired from a date (defaults to the sheet's today). A claim dated after a person's
retirement date is refused with an error; claims dated on or before it are allowed even if added
later. Retired people are left out of the list (no row for them on the screen at all) unless "show
retired" is on: a toggle on the screen, off when the screen is first opened and left as it is by
loading a sheet. Their claims keep counting in every total. Show retired yes/no and retired-from.
Retiring writes PERSON_RETIRED name=<name> from=<date>. A person with a retirement date set counts
as retired at once, whatever the date, even one after the sheet's today: the row shows retired yes,
the list hides it, and every rule that speaks of a retired person or member applies to them.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Retiring people now works: `bin/e2e` passes all 4 retire tests and the frontend type check is clean.

**What it does**
- Each person's row shows retired `yes`/`no` and the retired-from date, with a date box and a **Retire** button. A blank date means the sheet's today.
- A person counts as retired as soon as the date is set, even if the date is after the sheet's today.
- Retiring writes `PERSON_RETIRED sheet=… by=… name=… from=…` to the audit file.
- A claim dated after the person's retirement date is refused with an error. The same rule also applies when editing a claim's date and when using quick-add. Claims dated on or before the retirement date are still allowed.
- Retired people have no row unless the new **Show retired** toggle is on. It starts off and stays as it is when a sheet is loaded.
- Retired people's claims still count in every total.

**Changes**
- **Database:** a migration, `V16__person_retired.sql`, adds a `retired_from` column to people.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/retire`. The claim add, claim edit and quick-add endpoints each gained a step that checks the retirement date.
- **Front end:** a new `features/retire/` folder holds the row column and the toggle. The list hides retired people in `PeopleList` itself, so the totals still see everyone.

**One change to existing code you might not expect:** the Statement button's error (`person-error`) is now shared by the whole row and shown once at the end of it. If the Retire column had its own copy, a row would have two `person-error` elements and the test could never see a refusal. Any action on the row clears the error.
